name: Changwon Sculpture Biennale
funding: 2024: 107,710 visitors; run by Changwon City and Changwon Culture Foundation; backed by Culture Ministry, Gyeongnam, KICOX and BNK Kyongnam Bank.
watch: The 2026 edition (30 Sep-15 Nov) is open. The 2024 roster stands; names include BNK Kyongnam Bank and Gyeongnam Mecenat Association.
records_note: Parent Changwon Culture Foundation posts accounts 2016 to 2025 and officer rosters, but no annual reports or funder list.

name: Charleston
funding: Charity running Charleston farmhouse and its Wolfson Gallery. Gifts and grants from the Art Fund, National Lottery Heritage Fund and Arts Council England; Bloomberg Connects supplies its digital guide.
watch: Bloomberg Philanthropies runs Bloomberg Connects. More than 260 UK artists asked five London theatres to drop it in May 2026; Charleston was not named.
records_note: One annual report found (2023), accounts on the Charity Commission register, no standing funder list, and trustees named on the Team page.

name: CHAT (Centre for Heritage, Arts and Textile)
funding: Non-profit Mill6 Foundation, founded by Vanessa Cheung. Founding donor: D. H. Chen Foundation. Main donor: Nan Fung Group, the property group that owned the mills.
watch: Opened 16 March 2019 in a former Nan Fung cotton mill. ANTEPRIMA partners on the textile art prize.
records_note: No annual report or accounts; it names two donors, undated, and lists eight directors of Mill 6 Foundation, mostly Nan Fung Group executives.

name: Cheongju Craft Biennale
funding: 2025: city-run (committee chaired by Cheongju's mayor) with national Korea Art Festival support; partners Hyundai Motor, Genesis, Hyundai Department Store, Aero K, Emart24.
watch: Hyundai Motor, a 2025 partner: its subsidiary SMART Alabama hired children as young as 12 (Reuters, 2022). Over 400,000 visitors in 2025.
records_note: Its site failed a certificate check; searches found only press coverage of the organizing committee, no reports, accounts, donors or board.

name: Chillida Leku
funding: Run by the Chillida estate in partnership with Hauser & Wirth.
records_note: Its site shows sponsorship tiers from 2,000 euros a year but names no funders, and posts no reports, accounts or board.

name: Chinati Foundation
watch: Founded by Donald Judd in Marfa, Texas. Preserves large-scale installations across 340 acres.
records_note: Its Financial Information page posts audited statements and Form 990s for 2016 to 2024, and a Trustees page names 19; it names no donors.

name: CIAP
funding: Flemish Community Cultural Department, City of Genk; non-profit contemporary art association.
watch: On C-mine, a former coal mining site; its programme deals with ecology after extraction.

name: Cité internationale des arts
funding: A public-benefit foundation funded by France's Ministry of Culture, the City of Paris and the Académie des Beaux-Arts, plus about 135 partners who rent studios.
watch: 310 live-in studios in the Marais and Montmartre. Corporate patrons are Samsung Foundation of Culture, Icatu and Neuflize OBC.
records_note: The Cité posts annual reports for 2023 to 2025, a named partner list and its board, but no financial statements.

name: Coaxial Arts Foundation
funding: California Arts Council, Department of Cultural Affairs City of Los Angeles (DCA), Andy Warhol Foundation; 501(c)(3) non-profit.
watch: Artist-run non-profit space on South Main Street dedicated to experimental video, sound art, and live media performance.

name: Colección de Arte Amalia Lacroze de Fortabat
funding: Private museum run by the Fundación Amalia Lacroze de Fortabat, set up by the Loma Negra cement heiress.
watch: Opened October 2008 in a Rafael Viñoly building. A 2014 prosecutors' office report said Loma Negra, which the founder controlled, gained from the 1976 coup.
records_note: The collection publishes no annual reports, accounts, sponsor list or foundation board; its institutional page names only staff.

name: Colección FEMSA
funding: Corporate art collection of FEMSA, founded 1977 and managed by FEMSA staff. FEMSA runs OXXO stores and the Coca-Cola FEMSA bottler.
watch: Residents of San Cristóbal de las Casas, Chiapas marched in 2017 to cancel the Coca-Cola FEMSA plant's water concession; permits cost 2,600 pesos each.
records_note: The collection is part of FEMSA, which files an annual report and a 20-F with audited accounts and names its board.

name: Colomboscope
funding: Run by the independent Fold Media Collective. Named: founding partners Goethe-Institut, British Council and Alliance Française, plus individual Friends. The page's 33 partner and patron logos carry no names.
watch: Cinnamon Hotels was title sponsor in the 2010s. The Gujral Foundation is a long-term partner. The ASAP grant in the old text is not found.
records_note: Its Partners page names founding partners and eleven Friends in text, undated; most patron logos have no names, and no reports, accounts or board.
